## Design

### 2026-10-29: This week was quite a long but productive one as I continued working on our ShakeMe project. I spent a lot time working on the PCB design, and it was a process filled with planning, adjustments, and p

**15h**

This week was quite a long but productive one as I continued working on our ShakeMe project. I spent a lot time working on the PCB design, and it was a process filled with planning, adjustments, and problem-solving. Although I faced a few challenges, I eventually managed to complete the design.

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 21-36-41](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/5cee230d73dcb4974c5e089d686dc79829999d1701735a91cbf7f34896f11b00.png)

One of my first challenges was figuring out how to arrange all the components without making the device too large. Initially, I planned to place everything on the front side of the PCB, but I realised that this would take up too much space. So, I came up with the idea of using both sides of the board.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/bf028727de9891b0db7fc0a6da71cb842ab0913701c587db03fe6115368ba00f.png)

At first, the idea seemed promising, but things didn't go as smoothly as expected. I tried about three different designs, but the component pins kept interfering with one another. Since I wanted to keep the PCB compact, finding a suitable arrangement was quite challenging.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/4fe565e480d4ac9c70fd9dbe2f46d41c783df18ea98c27ef320208c5ff316276.png)

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 13-45-09](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/99a08c53bddf753bfef2a8ace58961bfc4d9ff2c4508b0805ce30d14bcc4d604.png)

After several attempts, we finally came up with a better design that solved the pin interference problem. I carefully rearranged the components to ensure they fitted properly without affecting one another. This was a major breakthrough because it allowed me to move forward with the design.

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 13-45-09](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/99a08c53bddf753bfef2a8ace58961bfc4d9ff2c4508b0805ce30d14bcc4d604.png)

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 15-05-07](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/2e1ce43ddc4f1ec0ff263a91b81f94f0a485c4fad4a9adc11c3c043430f11a27.png)

Another challenge was finding the correct component footprints, symbols, and 3D models. Some of the models we needed weren't available in the libraries I checked, so I had to spend extra time searching for suitable alternatives. Eventually, I was able to resolve the issue and continue with the design.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/219f9bcd776a5f81499cad9d4bcd540d4913d10bba9f1ff523f09c6e2b8bb237.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/038b762373b3f4515f2f7ff69510ed532ff1f925ea9ce151e005ed84483f134d.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/f04724ed1793d4f3baf81989de62bc045626250a0830a39ebf94baa858941645.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/c0e26ff43a5b0cc9ed26f969a4acceda4b6accc5843725c42b446846ab6f5ea7.png)

Routing also gave me some trouble during the process. Connecting the components properly while keeping the board neat required careful planning. I eventually worked through this by using two layers: a ground layer and a power layer for the 3.3 V supply, which helped me organise the connections.

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 21-37-38](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/24e461ca77993e54e539c52e1533f6200e02ee1f97ada7e5feaaf4269a0128fe.png)

By the end of the session, I had completed the PCB design. It was satisfying to see how we went from struggling with component placement to finding a layout that worked. The proces

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 13-46-00](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/efcc3211a282aa92aae8973c8fb6e54a4b8f1043c484a09a179b1f913d70b8a0.png)

![Screenshot from 2026-10-28 21-33-42](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/83wHhG3lcEmAv3SucuBTvqFHVoYz3xIc/a9ceed618944cba6d983679a711bb3fd01e828a5a9c5e854ede0bfa09d553a57.png)

Overall, these 15 hours taught me a lot about PCB layout, component placement, footprints, 3D models, and routing. I also learned that the first design doesn't always work out, and sometimes the best solution comes after several attempts. Now that the PCB design is complete, I'm looking forward to moving on to the next stage of the project.
